cards.explanation: The answer is True. Romans 9:30 says it plainly: the Gentiles, the people who aren't Israelites, "…did not pursue righteousness…" and still "…have obtained it…" That sounds backward, like winning a race you never signed up for. But the verse says it, and it adds what kind of righteousness it is: one that is by faith. Hold onto that last part, friends, because the whole passage leans on it.

The answer is a righteousness by faith. That's the phrase Paul uses in Romans 9:30: "…a righteousness that is by faith…" Notice what the Gentiles didn't bring to the table, friends. The verse says they did not pursue righteousness, so faith is the only word it gives for how they got it.

The answer is False. Paul says Israel "…has not attained it." (Romans 9:31) Israel pursued a law of righteousness, so the effort was there. It's like me chasing the last cookie crumb across the counter with my mustache and still coming up empty. The verse sets up the next question, which is why.

The answer is that they pursued it as if by works. That's Paul's answer in Romans 9:32: "Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works." The pursuit was there, but it wasn't by faith. Notice the words "as if," friends. Paul says it was as if it were by works.

The answer is that they will never be put to shame. Paul quotes Isaiah, a prophet, and the quote ends: “…the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.” (Romans 9:33) The stone makes some people stumble, but the one who believes in Him never gets put to shame. That's a promise worth keeping close, bakers. It shows up again in Romans 10:11.

The answer is salvation. Paul says, "…my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their salvation." (Romans 10:1) He addresses them as brothers, and then he opens up. That's not a lecture, friends, it's a prayer. I think you can hear how much he means it.

The answer is False. Paul says they're zealous for God, "…but not on the basis of knowledge." (Romans 10:2) He vouches for their zeal first. Then he says it didn't rest on knowledge. Both parts are in the same verse, friends.

The answer is that they did not submit to it. Paul says they "…did not submit to God’s righteousness." (Romans 10:3) They were ignorant of it and sought to establish their own. Submitting means going along with God's way instead of building your own. I once decided to stamp a whole batch my way instead of the way that works, bakers. The cookies came out as blobs.

The answer is Christ. Paul writes, "…Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes." (Romans 10:4) Notice the end of that sentence, friends: righteousness for everyone who believes. That's the bridge from Israel's chase to the righteousness that comes by faith. Everything else in the passage hangs on this one verse.

The answer is that it would be to bring Christ down. Paul says that asking who will ascend into heaven would be "…to bring Christ down…" (Romans 10:6) The righteousness by faith says not to say it in your heart. Heights and I don't mix anyway, friends. My base is gold, but it's not a rocket.

The answer is that the word is near you. The text says, “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart…” (Romans 10:8) Nobody has to climb up to heaven or dig down to the Abyss to find it. It's closer than that, friends. Paul calls it "…the word of faith we are proclaiming…"

The answers are mouth and heart. Paul says you are saved if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord (Romans 10:9). The mouth is where the confessing happens, and verse 10 repeats it: "…with your mouth you confess and are saved." So the first blank is mouth. The verse also says you "…believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead…" (Romans 10:9), and verse 10 backs it up: "…with your heart you believe and are justified…" So the second blank is heart. The belief is on the inside and the confession is on the outside, bakers.

The answer is False. Paul says "…there is no difference between Jew and Greek…" (Romans 10:12) The reason is that the same Lord is Lord of all. One Lord, one counter, same welcome for everybody in line, friends.

The answer is richly. Paul says the same Lord "…gives richly to all who call on Him…" (Romans 10:12) Richly isn't a small word, friends. It means the giving isn't thin or stingy. And it goes to all who call on Him.

The answer is someone to preach. Paul asks, "…how can they hear without someone to preach?" (Romans 10:14) It's a chain, friends, and this link is that someone has to speak. Calling needs believing, believing needs hearing, and hearing needs a preacher. Take out one link and the chain drops.

The answer is sent. Paul asks, "…how can they preach unless they are sent?" (Romans 10:15) Preaching has a sender behind it, friends. Then he quotes Isaiah, a prophet, about the beautiful feet of those who bring good news. That's the next link in the chain, and it's a good one.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…not all of them welcomed the good news." (Romans 10:16) He backs it up with Isaiah, a prophet, who asks, “Lord, who has believed our message?” The claim in the verse is that not all of them welcomed it, friends.

The answer is by hearing the word of Christ. Paul sums it up: “…faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.” (Romans 10:17) That's where the chain he's been building lands, friends. Faith comes by hearing, and the hearing is by the word of Christ. It's why the preaching mattered so much.

The answer is True. Paul says Isaiah, a prophet, boldly says, “I was found by those who did not seek Me; I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.” (Romans 10:20) So yes, found by those who did not seek. Paul calls it bold, friends, and I'd say the word fits.

The answer is holding out His hands to them. The line says, “All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.” (Romans 10:21) Hands held out, and all day long. I think that picture is hard to forget, friends. Paul says it's what is said about Israel.
